answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after completing tasks that recipients confirm, with each bond locked until the work is checked. A new identity must therefore post its own stake and build a record; splitting into many accounts does not multiply influence unless each account pays that cost and delivers useful work. An attacker may wander from a terrace of cheap identities to saffron-colored profiles, but every one still needs capital at risk and independent confirmations, making mass Sybils expensive to sustain.
